body.estimand_functional: \(R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), where \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\) is the independently defined Airy value and is to be certified by the corrected all-count diagonal

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including dependence across labeled units and zero allocation to an arm. The proved comparator assigns units independently with \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\). The corrected prior is selected independently of the design, and the orbit reduction is exact at every fixed allocation count; uniform optimization over all counts remains open.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population of \(n\) labeled units with three binary potential outcomes; the exact response-count orbit retains all eight response types.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one of three arm labels is assigned to each unit, and the observation is the assigned label together with its binary outcome.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed on the unrestricted design. Positive local counts, positive exterior counts, and zero-count faces are separate required conclusions of the corrected bridge, so boundary allocations cannot be discarded by assumption.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation. The compact transverse coordinate is a design-independent prior device orthogonal to the finite-population contrast; shrinking it while retaining uniform control of posterior denominators and allocation boundaries is part of the open proof.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The unrestricted two-arm binary minimax risk equals \(n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and is attained by Bernoulli randomization with nonlinear shrinkage.
For the two-arm bounded-outcome game, independent assignment remains minimax when estimators are unrestricted.
Under permutation-invariant law classes and linear estimation schemes, complete randomization with Neyman allocation is minimax.
A first-order local asymptotic minimax bound applies across broad sequential experimental designs, including multiple treatments.
Pairwise-independent inclusion attains the sharp bounded-total minimax risk within the class of unbiased estimators.
Limits of experiments yield asymptotically optimal treatment rules under average and minimax risk criteria in smooth models.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.

body.tldr: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the proved sharp result is currently the fixed-independent-design expansion with coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), together with the corresponding one-sided lower limit for the unrestricted deficit. The former widening polynomial tube is exactly refuted. Its replacement is an effective compact rational Airy spline-square prior: a rational interval ODE/Taylor oracle certifies normalized energy and weighted tails, and a fixed-input evaluator computes exact ordered-field Bayes intervals and finite allocation-stratum maxima. The sharp-limit and effective-certificate nodes are now faithful corollaries of the corrected allocation-tube conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\); because that all-count bridge remains open, the unrestricted sharp equality is not yet established.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent proves the \(n^{-4/3}\) order and finite response-type programs, while the proved fixed-independent theorem identifies the Airy coefficient. No available result gives the reverse inequality for every outcome-independent dependent design. The missing step is a uniform corrected-prior Bayes bridge covering \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation perturbations, all positive-count exterior allocations, and zero-count faces with one effective remainder.
project_justification.niche: At \(c^\dagger\), all eight response types and a nonzero transverse nuisance direction are needed because a scalar-path prior can be exploited by a pair-focused design. The scientifically meaningful unresolved question is whether unrestricted designs improve on the fixed allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) at second order.
project_justification.fill: The current verified contribution gives the exact response-alphabet geometry, a total fixed-independent Airy procedure, an effective normalized rational Airy-record algorithm, a genuine corrected transverse prior at every admissible input, an exact permutation-orbit Bayes reduction, and a terminating same-input ordered-algebraic evaluator. The proposed root theorem states the precise all-count inequalities, four certified errors, and monotone tail certificate still needed; its dependent sharp-limit and effective-certificate nodes now expose only the consequences of those corrected conclusions.

body.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) provide the scalar two-arm Airy benchmark and feedback bounds, not a three-active-arm all-design converse. Hull (2026) is likewise a two-arm unrestricted result. The accepted parent supplies the exact finite orbit game, first-order value, second-order order, and same-sample rational certificate sandwiches. The present verified machinery gives the effective normalized rational Airy record, exact corrected tube prior, permutation-orbit Bayes reduction, and same-input evaluator; it does not supply the uniform all-count asymptotic bridge. Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) inform the limiting decision and spectral architecture. Bai (2023), Armstrong (2022), and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) concern related randomization or allocation restrictions but do not settle this unrestricted second-order game. Hammer et al. (1996) supplies only the prospective complete binary-endpoint regimen-trial motivation; no censored-outcome reanalysis is claimed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(K=3,n=3\) full-label risk \(511653/4000000\) is below the scalar Bayes lower value \(18213/136000\), but this does not establish an asymptotic gap. A longitudinal-only prior is defeated by a pair-focused design, and the former widening polynomial prior is refuted by its exact Bayes-risk calculation. The rational Airy replacement fixes normalized longitudinal energy measured through the quotient and is effective at every fixed input, but finite enumeration cannot prove a common future-sample tail. The remaining task is a likelihood or Bayes-information expansion uniform over local counts, exterior shells, posterior denominators, and zero-count faces. Published comparator; no novelty claimed: for support two, direct evaluation gives \(\kappa(c)=1\) and the published two-arm coefficient \(C_A\).
body.honest_scope: The root bridge is confined to \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) with fixed three-arm support. Unconditionally proved results include the fixed-independent expansion with coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\), its total finite procedure, the one-sided unrestricted lower limit, the effective normalized Airy-record algorithm, and fixed-input corrected Bayes and primal certificates. The unrestricted sharp equality and its cross-sample effective certificate remain dependent on the open allocation-tube conclusions. No growing-arm, uniform vanishing-weight, or arbitrary-real computability claim is made, and equality versus strict second-order loss for the independent design remains unresolved.
body.interpretation: A prospective trialist can use the proved fixed-independent allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\), its total Airy-feedback estimator, and the terminating same-input certificate machinery for the finite-population contrast. The reauthored sharp-limit theorem shows exactly how the corrected Bayes certificate, four errors, and computable tail would yield an unrestricted sharp benchmark. Until the allocation-tube root is proved, that conditional squeeze must not be presented as evidence that dependent designs have no second-order advantage.
